name: Priority Access
tagline: Protect reserved, accessible, and VIP access before general vehicle fallbacks.
brief: Route reserved, accessible, VIP, electric, large, and standard vehicles in safe priority order.
context: Reserved pass holders, mobility permit holders, and VIP arrivals share the queue with ordinary traffic.
narrative:
Priority vehicles have joined the entrance queue!

Reserved pass holders require their designated spot, mobility permit holders require accessible bays, and VIP guests expect premium spaces.

Build a priority rule hierarchy: handle exit requests, then reserved (carReserved), accessible (carAccessible), and VIP (carVIP) rules before checking electric, large, or standard fallbacks.
objective: Serve all ten vehicles and keep every protected category correctly matched.
learningObjective: Build an ordered rule hierarchy that guarantees access rights before general resource allocation.
intelligenceExplanation:
Place special access rules above general vehicle rules so protected categories get their dedicated spaces.

Recommended order:
1. WHEN hasExitRequest -> DO release-vehicle
2. WHEN carReserved -> DO park-reserved
3. WHEN carAccessible -> DO park-accessible
4. WHEN carVIP -> DO park-premium
5. WHEN carElectric -> DO park-charging
6. WHEN carLarge -> DO park-large
7. WHEN hasWaitingVehicle -> DO park-standard
hint: Order: release -> reserved -> accessible -> VIP -> electric -> large -> standard.
hints: Place carReserved, carAccessible, and carVIP rules above carElectric and carLarge.
